title: Quandela Establishes South Korea as Asian Hub for Photonic QPU Manufacturing and Hardware R&D - Quantum Computing Report
gist: French photonic QPU maker Quandela is making South Korea its Asian hub for QPU manufacturing and R&D, seeking a consortium with Samsung, SK hynix and LG Innotek, partnering with KAIST and KRIBB, aligning with Seoul's ₩80B MOU, and citing NVIDIA NVQLink work that cut GPU-to-QPU latency to milliseconds.

themes.theme: Korea as photonic QPU manufacturing hub

insights.claim: Quandela aims to form an industrial consortium with South Korean foundries such as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix and optoelectronic integrators like LG Innotek to mass-produce photonic control chips and optical packaging.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Korean semiconductor majors could gain quantum-photonics exposure; note the consortium is 'sought', not signed.
insights.quote: to scale mass production of photonic control chips and optical component packaging
insights.locator: The manufacturing strategy seeks to form

insights.claim: Under the proposed IP framework, pre-existing IP stays with each partner, while co-developed manufacturing protocols and optical modules are shared according to contributions.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IP terms determine who captures value from cross-border manufacturing partnerships.
insights.locator: The manufacturing strategy seeks to form

insights.claim: Quandela Korea plans to grow from 3 to 10 systems engineers by 2027 in alignment with a Seoul Metropolitan Government ₩80B MOU for a regional QPU cluster.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Small headcount numbers show the hub is early-stage despite the strategic framing.

insights.claim: KAIST engineering teams are deploying to Paris to integrate Korean-fabricated electronic control units into Quandela's QPU chassis, creating a cross-border supply chain for FTQC.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Europe-Korea quantum supply chains diversify away from U.S.-China dependencies.

insights.claim: KRIBB will run proof-of-concept photonic QPU molecular simulation for drug discovery.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Early application POCs in pharma; commercially immaterial for now.

insights.claim: Working with NVIDIA via NVQLink, Quandela reduced GPU-to-QPU communication latency from tens of seconds to the millisecond scale, enabling hybrid error mitigation across HPC clusters such as the 12-qubit Lucy processor at France's TGCC.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: NVIDIA's NVQLink is becoming a de facto integration layer across QPU vendors, reinforcing NVIDIA's position in hybrid quantum computing.
insights.quote: Reduced GPU-to-QPU communication latency from tens of seconds to the millisecond (ms) scale
